column1: # Estate baseline anchors — the best prior evidence that read each repository
# FROM ITS OWN SOURCE, and the instant it measured.
# baseline_utc is the START of the measurement day: an audit written on the
# 22nd read a tree that existed that day, so taking the day's end would
# silently absorb same-day commits the audit never saw.
# certainty is the PRIOR evidence's own rating, not this run's.  It is the
# judgement half of the classification and is applied by the reader; delta.py
# decides only UNCHANGED vs CHANGED, which is a fact about the tree.
# baseline_sha is THIS RUN'S measurement point — the commit the 2026-09-04 audit
# actually read (a re-audited repository's own `sha_verified`, otherwise the
# pinned tip it was classified against). A later delta compares FROM here.
# It is deliberately NOT the old date-derived baseline. Two rounds were needed to
# get this right: round 2 added the column, round 3 caught that it had been filled
# from `delta.tsv`'s `baseline_commit` — the point the PRIOR evidence measured —
# so `couch-legend` read 43bc12865786 where the audit had read d877ed0b6114. That
# would leave every later run comparing from an obsolete point: an unchanged tip
# reads CHANGED_REAUDIT forever, and a reset back to the old baseline reads
# UNCHANGED_REUSABLE. `baseline_utc` and `evidence_ref` still describe the PRIOR
# evidence; this column describes what replaced it.
